label: Встать
description: A 10-sentence conjugation card for встать (to get up, to stand up).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Perfective future, first-person. Встать is perfective, so 'встану' carries future meaning with the present-like ending -у on the stem встан-. 'Завтра' fixes the time of the single act.

missions.phrase: Ты встанешь и пойдёшь со мной.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Perfective future, second-person. 'Встанешь' shows the -ешь ending on the stem встан-. Being perfective, it denotes one completed getting-up before the next action 'пойдёшь'.
Strategic focus: Perfective future, third-person. 'Встанет' is the он-form ending in -ет. The phrase 'в шесть часов' marks the exact moment of the single completed action.
Strategic focus: Perfective future, first-person plural. 'Встанем' is the мы-form ending in -ем on the stem встан-. The perfective frames a single planned departure.
Strategic focus: Perfective future, third-person plural. 'Встанут' closes the future ladder with the -ут ending. It describes one collective act of standing up.
Strategic focus: Masculine past tense. 'Встал' is the masculine singular past of perfective встать, reporting a single completed rising. The imperfective partner вставать would stress habit.
Strategic focus: Feminine past tense. 'Встала' adds the feminine -а ending. Two perfectives in a row, 'встала' then 'открыла', show a clear sequence of finished actions.
Strategic focus: Plural past tense. 'Встали' is the plural past ending in -и. The phrase 'из-за стола' shows the common idiom for getting up from the table.

missions.phrase: Каждый день я встаю в семь.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Imperfective present partner. Here the imperfective вставать gives 'встаю', the habitual я-form. It contrasts with perfective встать and is needed for the repeated daily routine.
Strategic focus: Singular imperative. 'Встань' is the informal command of perfective встать, built on the stem встан-. It demands one immediate completed action.
